subject: Meteorology
title: The Anemometer
description: A quick win: understand The Anemometer.

hook.text: Leon Battista Alberti described an early wind-measuring device in 1450—a swinging plate pushed by the wind.

buildup.text: The cup anemometer arrived in 1846, invented by John Robinson—spinning cups whose rotation speed indicates wind speed.

discovery.text: The Beaufort scale, created in 1805 by Francis Beaufort, categorized wind by its effects—from calm to hurricane force.

twist.text: Beaufort originally described wind effects on sailing ships—it was later adapted to effects on land and sea conditions.

climax.text: Modern sonic anemometers have no moving parts—they measure wind by timing sound pulses between transducers.

punchline.text: From swinging plates to sound waves—tracking the invisible force.

quiz.question: Who created the wind force scale still used in modified form today?
